title: Distributed Systems
tagline: Failure models, remote communication, time and clocks, replication and consistency, consensus, fault tolerance, distributed storage, distributed transactions and data processing
summary: Modern services run on many machines that fail independently and communicate over unreliable networks. This course covers the foundations of building such systems: models of failure and timing, remote communication, time and logical clocks, replication and consistency models, consensus with Paxos and Raft, fault tolerance, distributed storage and transactions, and large-scale data processing.

chapters.title: Models of distributed systems
chapters.summary: Why systems are distributed, failure models, assumptions about timing, and the fallacies of distributed computing.

chapters.title: Communication and remote procedure calls
chapters.summary: Message passing, remote procedure calls, serialisation and idempotence.

chapters.title: Time, clocks and ordering
chapters.summary: Physical clock synchronisation, Lamport clocks, vector clocks and causality.

chapters.title: Replication and consistency
chapters.summary: Primary–backup and quorum replication, linearisability, eventual consistency and the CAP theorem.

chapters.title: Consensus
chapters.summary: The consensus problem, the FLP impossibility result, Paxos and Raft.

chapters.title: Fault tolerance
chapters.summary: Failure detection, state-machine replication, Byzantine faults and recovery.

chapters.title: Distributed storage
chapters.summary: Partitioning and consistent hashing, distributed file systems and key–value stores.

chapters.title: Distributed transactions
chapters.summary: Two-phase commit, distributed concurrency control and globally consistent databases.

chapters.title: Large-scale data processing
chapters.summary: MapReduce, dataflow systems and stream processing.
